title: Bankruptcy (Estate Charges) Amendment (Norfolk Island) Bill 2020
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would extend Commonwealth bankruptcy estate charges to Norfolk Island as part of a package extending the national personal insolvency framework to the island.
Removing the territorial exclusion would allow charges on insolvency realisations and interest earned on money held in personal insolvency accounts to apply there.
It would commence with Schedule 3 of the Territories Legislation Amendment Bill 2020, and would not commence if that companion schedule did not commence.
changes: The express exclusion of Norfolk Island from the estate charges legislation would be repealed.
Realisations charges could be imposed on covered Norfolk Island insolvencies.
Interest charges could also be collected on those administrations.
summary.affected: Trustees, debt agreement administrators and people in covered Norfolk Island personal insolvency arrangements are affected.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The Bankruptcy (Estate Charges) Amendment (Norfolk Island) Bill extends the 1997 Act to Norfolk Island, ensuring consistent estate charges and equal treatment for bankruptcies there as in the rest of Australia.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Territories Legislation Amendment Bill 2020 and the Bankruptcy (Estate Charges) Amendment (Norfolk Island) Bill, arguing they ensure consistent Commonwealth support and law application for external territories. Labor moved a second reading amendment urging proper consultation with community stakeholders and the legal profession, including the Law Association of Norfolk Island and the Law Council of Australia.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the Territories Legislation Amendment Bill and associated bankruptcy bill would align Norfolk Island and other territories with mainland Australia on governance, legal frameworks, and services. The speaker noted the bills extend national company and bankruptcy laws to Norfolk Island, improve privacy rights and review opportunities for residents, and ensure easier access to future government support packages.
